name: openat2
synopsis: long syscall(SYS_openat2, int dirfd, const char *pathname, struct open_how *how, size_t size);
description: The openat2() system call extends openat(2) by providing a superset of its functionality through an extensible structure. It opens the file specified by pathname, optionally creating it if O_CREAT is specified, and allows advanced path resolution options. If pathname is relative, it is resolved relative to the directory referred to by dirfd.

parameters.name: dirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor; if AT_FDCWD, uses the current working directory; ignored for absolute pathnames unless specified otherwise.

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.description: Path to the file to open.

parameters.name: how
parameters.description: Pointer to a structure specifying flags, mode, and resolution options for opening the file.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Size of the struct open_how structure, used for extensibility and version checking.

return_value.success: Returns a new file descriptor on success
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: An extension that this kernel does not support was specified in how.
how.resolve contains either RESOLVE_IN_ROOT or RESOLVE_BENEATH, and the kernel could not ensure that a '..' component didn’t escape.
RESOLVE_CACHED was set, and the open operation cannot be performed using only cached information.
An unknown flag or invalid value was specified in how.
mode is nonzero, but how.flags does not contain O_CREAT or O_TMPFILE.
size was smaller than any known version of struct open_how.
how.resolve contains RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, and one of the path components was a symbolic link.
how.resolve contains RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS, and one of the path components was a magic link.
how.resolve contains either RESOLVE_IN_ROOT or RESOLVE_BENEATH, and an escape from the root during path resolution was detected.
how.resolve contains RESOLVE_NO_XDEV, and a path component crosses a mount point.
